weather noun

also the weather, good weather, bad weather, what’s the weather like, lousy weather, foul weather, climate, kinds of weather, depending on the weather, weather conditions, weather the storm, beautiful weather

classical

Caes. B.G. 4.23: nactus idōneam ad nāvigandum tempestātem (Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 2.2: tempestātēs malās fuisse
M-O s.v. weather
Traupman 137, 405

tempestās, tempestātis f.

noun, third declension

weather, good or bad

Weather is its chief classical sense (Lewis & Short), fair or foul: tempestās serēna, idōnea, turbida. Alone it very often means a storm (see storm), and in early Latin and the historians also a time (eā tempestāte, “at that time”), so give it an adjective when you mean fine weather.

Other words

  • caelum, caelī n. — the weather; the state of the sky

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 8.17.1: immīte et turbidum caelum; Col. 12.47.2: serēnō caelō; Traupman 292; Traupman 135, 405

    The sky, and so the weather it brings, especially weather that lasts (see climate). serēnō caelō, “in fine weather”.

  • spurcus, spurca, spurcum — foul, lousy (of weather)

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. fr. ap. Non. 394.9: tempestās spurcissima (Lewis & Short); Suet. Caes. 60: spurcātissimīs tempestātibus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 136

Examples

  • num istīc quoque immīte et turbidum caelum? hīc assiduae tempestātēs et crēbra dīluvia

    is the weather wild and stormy there too? here it is one storm after another, and floodsPlin. Ep. 8.17.1

  • intemperiēs caelī valētūdinem temptat: aegrōtandum est

    bad weather tries our health: we must be illSen. Ep. 107.7

  • nactus idōneam ad nāvigandum tempestātem

    having found weather fit for sailingCaes. B.G. 4.23 (Lewis & Short)

  • tempestās adversa (gravis)

    bad weatherTraupman 135

  • ut diēs suādet

    depending on the weatherTraupman 137

  • propter caelī varietātēs

    owing to changes in the weatherTraupman 137

  • tempestātēs

    kinds of weather; weather conditionsTraupman 405

  • ēgregia (clāra, serēna, nebulōsa, foeda, pluviōsa) tempestās

    beautiful (clear, fine, cloudy, foul, rainy) weatherTraupman 405

  • procellam dūrāre

    to weather the stormTraupman 405

  • rēs adversās superāre

    to weather the storm (figuratively)Traupman 405

See also climate, storm, clear sky, heat, weather forecast, sky.
